sections.h2: Where is the Union County Recorder's Office in Marysville?
sections.html:
The Union County Recorder works from the County Office Building at 233 West Sixth Street, Marysville, Ohio 43040. Hours run Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with the front desk at 937-645-3032. Its own page calls it the official land records office for real estate in the county.

Indexing is the core task. Each document is indexed so a searcher can trace a chain of title and see any debt that still attaches to the land. Images and indexes are online from 1995 forward, and the office has recently added grantor and grantee deed indexes from 1875 to 1994, mortgage indexes from 1944 to 1994 and miscellaneous indexes from 1960 to 1994. For older papers that are not digitized, staff can send copies by email, fax or mail.

The auditor and treasurer share the building, so a deed, a tax question and a filing can often be handled in one trip.

sections.h2: What does the Union County Recorder charge in fees?
sections.html:
Fees rose by $5 on January 1, 2025, after Senate Bill 94 allowed a document preservation surcharge under Ohio Revised Code 317.32. The county's chart groups deeds, mortgages, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts and powers of attorney under one rate: $39 up front, then $8 a page.

Union County Recorder fees from the county fee schedule
ServiceFee
Deed, mortgage or similar document, first two pages$39
Each added page$8
Marginal reference on a separate instrument$4 each, on top of the recording fee
Copy, per page$2
Certified copy$1 per document added to the copy fee
Document that is not conforming$20
Veterans' discharge papersNo fee

Source: Union County Recorder fee schedule.

The county's one-to-ten page chart prints $39 for one or two pages, $47 for three, $63 for five and $103 for ten. Plats and condominium drawings run $0.10 per square inch, on sheets sized 18 by 24 inches. Zoning resolutions are $50 and zoning amendments $20.

sections.h2: How does a Union County deed get to the recorder?
sections.html:
By mail, the recorder will file a conveyance only if the Auditor's stamp is already on it. That sets the order here: Auditor first, Recorder second.

  • The buyer or a representative submits the value statement that section 319.202 requires, on the state's DTE 100 form. An exempt transfer uses the exemption statement, DTE 100EX.
  • The Auditor collects the conveyance fee, posted at $4 per $1,000 of value.
  • The Auditor stamps the deed, and the Recorder files it.

The Auditor, Engineer and Recorder adopted a shared set of Real Estate Conveyance Standards on May 1, 2014, after public hearings in February and March of that year. Those standards are what all three offices apply to a deed, so have the attorney or title company check a draft against them. Separately, section 322.02 lets a county adopt a transfer tax, so confirm with the Auditor what applies.

The fee schedule also warns that a document showing a Social Security number will be refused unless an affidavit is attached (section 317.082), so scan the draft before it goes in.

sections.h2: What layout rules apply to papers filed in Union County?
sections.html:
The county's fee schedule treats a document that misses the state standard in section 317.114 as non-conforming and adds $20. It spells out four points:

  • Print no smaller than 10 point.
  • Three inches left blank at the top of page one.
  • A 1 inch margin on each side and the bottom of every page.
  • One and a half inches of space above the text on later pages.

Have the closing agent check a draft against those four points, since the surcharge applies to each filing that misses them.

sections.h2: Can Union County records be filed or watched online?
sections.html:
Yes, in part. As of July 15, 2024 the office accepts eRecorded filings that are not conveyances. The announcement covers non-conveyance filings, so ask the office how a deed should be submitted.

Residents can also sign up for a free fraud alert service. The recorder describes it as a notification service meant to help combat real estate fraud, and the Recorder page links to the sign-up details.

sections.h2: Which liens and releases show up in Union County records?
sections.html:
The fee schedule doubles as a list of the lien types that can attach to a property, which is useful when a title search turns something up. Federal tax liens and federal court judgment abstracts cost $5 to file, and a release of either costs $3. Several state liens are filed with no fee, including workers' compensation liens, Ohio EPA liens, franchise tax liens, personal property tax liens and unemployment compensation liens. A release, partial release or discharge of a franchise tax, personal property tax, tangible or intangible tax, or unemployment compensation lien costs $4.

Fixture-type UCC filings tied to land run $12, plus $4 per indexed name. Marginal references, the $4 charge that links a release or assignment to the original recorded mortgage, are billed on top of the normal recording fee. If you paid off a mortgage, check that the lender actually filed the release. An unreleased mortgage keeps appearing in the title search.

sections.h2: What is Union County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Union County covers 437 square miles in central Ohio, with Marysville as county seat and largest city. Wikipedia reports that the county took shape in 1820 from pieces of Franklin, Delaware, Madison and Logan counties, hence the name, and that the courthouse still in use was dedicated January 27, 1883. Part of Dublin and part of Plain City lie inside the county, and Richwood, Milford Center, Magnetic Springs and Unionville Center are villages. US 33 runs through Marysville, and Honda's Marysville Auto Plant and Scotts Miracle-Gro are among the large employers.

School districts named for the county include Marysville Exempted Village, Fairbanks, North Union, Triad, Jonathan Alder, Buckeye Valley, Elgin, Benjamin Logan and Dublin City.

The Census Bureau shows a fast-growing market:

  • Population estimate for 2025: 73,446, up 17.0 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Typical owned home value, 2020 to 2024: $344,900.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 79.2 percent among 24,232 households.
  • Median gross rent: $1,247 a month.
  • Median household income: $112,322.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 968.

For a home in a platted subdivision, have the title company pull the plat and recorded restrictions together with the deed.

faqs.q: What is the fee to record a deed in Union County, Ohio?
faqs.a: Two pages of deed cost $39, and each page past two adds $8. Every marginal reference is another $4, and a deed that fails the formatting standard is hit with $20. The Auditor's conveyance fee is a different payment.

faqs.q: Does the Union County Recorder accept deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Only when the Auditor's conveyance stamp is already affixed. The fee schedule spells this out, so take the deed to the Auditor first and mail the stamped original with the right payment.

faqs.q: What are the Union County Recorder's office hours?
faqs.a: Staff take walk-ins Monday to Friday between 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., at 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville. Call 937-645-3032 with questions.

faqs.q: Can I eRecord a deed in Union County?
faqs.a: The recorder began accepting eRecorded non-conveyance filings on July 15, 2024. For a deed, ask the office how to submit, since the Auditor's conveyance stamp has to be on it first.

faqs.q: What does the Union County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: On its conveyance standards page, the county shows a conveyance fee of $4 for each thousand dollars of value. Ask the Auditor's office about any per-parcel charge and any local transfer tax.
